content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Use Could I try and Can I have in a clothing shop. Model: “Could I try the medium blue shirt, please?” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use trying clothes on clearly and politely. One useful response is: “Could I try the medium blue shirt, please?” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where trying clothes on is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?
content_sections.title: Use it

language_focus: Use Could I try and Can I have in a clothing shop.
objectives: Use Could I try and Can I have in a clothing shop.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about trying clothes on.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about trying clothes on. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: What does the speaker want to try on?
listening.transcript: Could I try on this green jacket, please? Yes, the fitting room is there.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Link could I; use a polite rising tone on please. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Link could I; use a polite rising tone on please.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about trying clothes on.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using trying clothes on; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise trying clothes on?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: Could I try the medium blue shirt, please?

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about trying clothes on with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about trying clothes on. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: Could I try the medium blue shirt, please? Submit your draft first.
